title_q: “Let Me Pay You to Do What You're Already Doing”
length: about 2:00 as briefed; about 90 s with the trims in the decision
headline: He was already helping people in his own recovery. Someone at MHA said: let me pay you to do what you're already doing.
story: Cerell came to MHA through his own recovery. He wanted to give back, and did not know if he was qualified. At a job fair he told Cynthia his story, and she said “let me pay you to do what you're already doing.” The things he thought would stop him from getting a job are the things that let him help others.
It must feel warm, plain and hopeful. His answer to anyone who doubts recovery: stops, peaks, valleys, and “never giving up.”
